questions.q: Trace the succession of dynasties that ruled the Delhi Sultanate.
answer: Between 1206 and 1526 the Delhi Sultanate was ruled by five successive dynasties.

answer.text: The Mamluk or 'Slave' dynasty (1206–1290) included Qutbuddin Aibak, Iltutmish, Raziyya and Balban. It was followed by the Khaljis (1290–1320), whose greatest ruler was Alauddin Khalji, and the Tughluqs (1320–1414), including Muhammad bin Tughluq and Firuz Shah. The Sayyids (1414–1451) came next, and finally the Lodis (1451–1526).
The Sultanate ended in 1526, when Babur defeated Ibrahim Lodi at the First Battle of Panipat, founding the Mughal empire.

answer: Across these dynasties, Delhi grew from a regional capital into the centre of a vast empire.

questions.q: Explain the iqta system used by the Delhi Sultans.
answer: To govern a large territory, the Khalji and Tughluq Sultans relied on the iqta system.

answer.text: Military commanders were appointed as governors of territories called iqtas. The holder of an iqta was called a muqti or iqtadar.
The muqti collected the revenue of his iqta as salary and used it to maintain soldiers, whom he led into battle, and to keep law and order in his area.

To stop muqtis from becoming powerful and independent, their accounts were checked and they were transferred from one iqta to another. In this way the Sultans balanced delegation with central control.

questions.q: Describe the notable experiments of Alauddin Khalji and Muhammad bin Tughluq.

answer.text: He built a large standing army and, to pay it cheaply, introduced strict control over prices in the Delhi markets, fixing rates for grain, cloth and other goods. He also strengthened defences against repeated Mongol invasions and built the Alai Darwaza.

He attempted two bold but failed experiments. He shifted the capital from Delhi to Daulatabad in the Deccan to control the south, then reversed the move, causing great hardship. He also introduced a 'token' currency of cheap metal declared equal in value to silver coins; because it was easily forged, it had to be withdrawn.

answer: Both rulers were innovative, but their measures show the limits of the Sultanate's control.
